narrationScript: To make your programs truly interactive, you need to get input from the user. For this, C provides `scanf`. Like `printf`, it uses format specifiers. But `scanf` needs to know *where* in memory to store the input. This is the crucial role of the **address-of operator**, `&`. When you write `scanf("%i", &user_age);`, the `&` before `user_age` tells `scanf` to go to the memory location of the `user_age` variable and put the integer it just read there. Forgetting this `&` is a common, critical mistake! Without it, `scanf` tries to use the variable's *value* as a memory address, usually leading to an invalid memory access and a program crash, or 'segmentation fault.' Always remember `&` with `scanf` for basic data types!
